clue.text: A rug's available for the guard

indicators.note: available in the sense of freely put to new use, so these letters may be rearranged at will

parts.note: the letters of 'a rug's' with the S of the possessive kept

explanation.surface: A rug is on offer to whoever keeps watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available' is a loose anagram signal: ARUGS rearranged gives the answer. Argus, the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth, was set by Hera to guard Io.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Argus was the many-eyed watchman Hera posted over Io, hence any vigilant keeper.

clue.text: A growing collection of trunks

parts.note: trunks suggest luggage, but here they are tree trunks, living specimens planted together

explanation.surface: A pile of luggage that keeps getting bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: Trunks read as suitcases; 'growing' means alive and sprouting, not increasing.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden of trees cultivated for study.

clue.text: Sound director made fun of

indicators.note: Sound says the word for director is spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: a guide directs people

explanation.surface: A sound engineer, or a director, was mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule them, so guyed is past tense mocking.

clue.text: Leading force in attack at the sharp end

explanation.surface: Troops at the front of an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading troops in an offensive are its vanguard; literally the pointed tip of a lance is its head.

clue.text: Fruit that's under weight will get publicity

parts.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit
something under weight is light

explanation.surface: An underweight piece of fruit somehow attracts media attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the limelight means being the focus of public attention, as a stage spotlight once picked out a star.

clue.text: Little beast always to be found in bar

indicators.note: to be found in means the word for always sits inside the word for bar

parts.note: a let is an obstacle or hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'
ever means always

explanation.surface: A small animal is forever turning up in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare, a small creature.

clue.text: A girl will accept employment malpractices

indicators.note: will accept means the girl takes the other word inside her

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: A young woman will take a job despite shady dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuses are wrong or improper uses, abuses of practice.

clue.text: Given rotten roles — he just can't win!

indicators.note: rotten means the letters of roles are decayed into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor handed poor parts despairs of ever succeeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never wins is a failure, the defeated party.

clue.text: "A plate of turtle green and — " (Browning)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the missing word completes Robert Browning's line from The Pied Piper of Hamelin about turtle soup

explanation.surface: A quotation from Browning with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from The Pied Piper of Hamelin: the Mayor dreams of 'a plate of turtle, green and' sticky, describing turtle soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutinous means sticky and gluey, as thick turtle soup is.

clue.text: Meeting that's enough to test the patience of a saint

parts.note: to try someone is to test their patience
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A meeting so tedious it would exasperate even a holy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret rendezvous, especially between lovers.

clue.text: A horse doesn't eat foliage

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
a diner who doesn't eat the food leaves it

explanation.surface: A fussy horse refuses its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay leaves are the aromatic leaves of the laurel, so they are a kind of greenery.

clue.text: Room required for the boss by the end of May

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised ornamental knob

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of May

explanation.surface: A study space must be ready for the manager by late May.
explanation.definitionFit: A study is a room in a house set aside for reading and writing.

clue.text: Comment in court and up he gets!

explanation.surface: A remark made in court, after which someone stands up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added clause or observation attached to a verdict; it is also one who is mounted, up on a horse.

clue.text: Lie about transport control

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go around the second's

parts.note: to lie down is to rest
a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Someone tells a lie about how they got here and keeps their composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control, holding oneself in check.

clue.text: It's really great to have a couple of pupils entering the exam

indicators.note: entering means these pieces go into the middle of the exam word

parts.note: an exam is a test
L is the abbreviation for learner, a pupil, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A pair of students sitting the test is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'really great' is a superlative of size: the greatest in height.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in the sense of big or high, at its utmost degree, is the greatest in stature.

clue.text: Set about a man holding doctors up — it's sickening

indicators.note: about means the word for set goes around the A

parts.note: a lot is a set or batch of items

indicators.note: holding means the man contains the doctors

parts.note: he stands for a man

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for doctors is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, doctors

explanation.surface: A gang surrounds a man and pins the doctors; it is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only reverses in a down clue, where the word is read from the bottom. 'it's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means causing disgust or revulsion, so nauseating.

clue.text: Drink for the ship's crew?

parts.note: the sea is jocularly 'the drink' and port is a drink sailors might take; together they name a harbour town where crews come ashore

explanation.surface: Asking what beverage sailors get on board.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about a beverage; in fact 'the drink' is slang for the sea, and port is both a wine and a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A town with a harbour where ships dock is where a crew comes ashore.

clue.text: A despot in confusion may appear the exact opposite

indicators.note: confusion means the letters of 'a despot in' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tyrant thrown into disarray might seem his own reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link; 'confusion' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodes are places diametrically opposed on the globe, and so things directly contrary.

clue.text: Dealing with someone who is patient?

definitions.text: Dealing with someone who is patient?

parts.words: Dealing with someone who is patient?
parts.note: patient here is a noun, someone under medical care, and dealing with such a person is care by a doctor

explanation.surface: How to handle a person who waits calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' reads as the adjective meaning tolerant; it is the noun, a person being cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is both medical care given to a sick person and the manner of dealing with someone.

clue.text: Turn or intend to turn Communist

parts.note: to intend is to mean

indicators.note: to turn here means the word for Communist is read backwards

parts.note: Red is a common term for a Communist

explanation.surface: A wavering person is asked whether they mean to defect to Communism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' appears twice: first as the definition, then 'to turn' as the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A meander is a winding bend in a river, a twist or curve in a course.

clue.text: Desert folk struggle to succeed

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side
a race is a people or folk

explanation.surface: Nomadic people of the Sahara battling to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the fierce competitive scramble for wealth and position.

clue.text: Some upstart is tearing into a performer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A young upstart rips into a stage entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'into a performer' cannot replace the answer; 'into' is a link joining the wordplay to 'a performer'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Reckon a foreign aristocrat to be about a hundred

indicators.note: to be about means the a-and-aristocrat pair goes around the hundred

parts.note: a count is a continental nobleman; Britain has earls instead
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Estimating that a European noble is nearly a hundred years old.
explanation.definitionFit: To account something so is to consider or judge it, as to reckon.

clue.text: According to plan, there's to be a new form of catechism

indicators.note: a new form of the word catechism means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church teacher plans to revise the catechism.
explanation.definitionFit: Schematic means laid out as a diagram or outline, so arranged to a set scheme.

clue.text: A note quickly written

explanation.surface: A memo jotted down in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written' is a link; a sharp is the symbol a composer writes to raise a note, and 'look sharp' means move quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a sharp is a note raised a semitone; as an adverb it means briskly or promptly.

clue.text: Covering that's not uniform

parts.note: uniform here is service dress, so clothing that isn't regulation dress is plain civilian wear

explanation.surface: A coat of paint applied unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not uniform' suggests uneven; it means not military dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is civilian clothing worn by someone usually in service uniform.

clue.text: Assume one is in the mail

indicators.note: is in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: post is the mail
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Presuming that one letter is already in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a premise, to suppose something for argument's sake.

clue.text: Divine substance

explanation.surface: Something holy and material.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to perceive intuitively; substance is the gist or meaning of what is said.

clue.text: Not at all concerned when a trick backfired

indicators.note: backfired means the word for trick goes backwards, a play on a plan rebounding

parts.note: to fool someone is to trick them

explanation.surface: Someone stays unbothered when a prank goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and uninvolved, cool and detached from others.

clue.text: A bad nun upset the Church plenty!

indicators.note: upset means the letters of 'a bad nun' are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A naughty nun has scandalised the clergy a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a great quantity, more than enough.

clue.text: A top man parking and staying

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
someone staying in a place is resident there

explanation.surface: A senior figure who parks his car and remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or organisation, its chief person.

clue.text: Quite small in a way, but very agreeable

indicators.note: in means the word for small goes inside the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: Something modest in size yet very pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet describes something pleasing or charming.
